question: Little Andaman in the south is separated from the Nicobar Islands by the ______.
solution:
The correct answer is the __10° channel__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• The Ten Degree Channel, which is about **90 miles (145 kilometers)** wide, separates Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the south.
 
• The union territory of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands is made up of two groups of islands off the coast of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Between Myanmar (Burma) and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, the peaks of a submerged mountain range, the Andaman Islands, and their southern neighbors, the Nicobar Islands, form an arc extending 620 miles (1,000 km) southward.
 
• The arc marks the western border of the Bay of Bengal and the eastern border of the Andaman Sea. 
 
• Port Blair is the territorial capital (on South Andaman Island).
 
• The islands are home to the Andaman and Nicobar Command, the Indian Armed Forces' only tri-service geographical command.
 
• According to the **2011 Indian Census**, the **Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands** had a population of **379,944**, with 202,330 men (53.25 percent) and 177,614 women (46.75 percent).
 
• There were 878 females for every 1,000 males. The Nicobar Islands are home to just 10% of the population.
